requirements.statement: Every passage a run reviews ends that run true of the code, or cut
Review effort follows the likely impact of recent commits on each doc
PRDs, TRDs and loose docs are each reviewed by a procedure that fits their structure
A PRD index and a TRD index match the tree after every run
Docs are tied to the code they describe by a coarse map
Nothing is removed that cannot be recovered
The file list covers every file under docs/ in the checked-out tree, of any type
Every file carries exactly one class: PRD, TRD or loose doc. Folder proposes, structure confirms; disagreement reported as loose doc
The commit list is every commit on checked-out branch after last-run marker. No marker → comprehensive run
Each file marked tracked, untracked or git-ignored
Assembly step makes no model call; identical inputs give identical output
For each PRD and TRD, Haiku produces impact score from commit list and doc
Score above high → Opus audit; medium → Sonnet once-over; low → no review
Both thresholds tunable settings. Defaults: high ≥ 70, medium ≥ 40 on 0–100 scale
Change set shows each doc's score and the depth it received
Run records where it got to (last-run marker) so next run knows which commits are new
Light run and comprehensive run each started by explicit invocation
Fan-out workflow consumes F1 output and F2 scores; does not re-decide class or depth
Each run behaves as specified (light: commits + scores; comprehensive: every PRD/TRD at least Sonnet)
Run with no last-run marker is comprehensive run, delivered in batches
Reports per requirement: built as stated, built differently, or not built
Requirement built differently is corrected to as-built
Requirement not built is surfaced to owner in change set rather than cut
How PRD claims checked against code (reuse of /audit-prd verifier or full audit) is TRD's decision
Tasks and decisions identified by structure and checked against code
Status that does not match what was delivered is corrected
How TRD claims checked against code (reuse of /audit-trd verifier or full audit) is TRD's decision
Prose loose docs describing system checked for unsupported claims and handled by F7
Non-text files (images, data) kept or removed, never corrected; removed only when reference check finds no use
For each section: code-shown-different content corrected; non-existent content cut; valid content left alone
Doc stays with valid content remaining however little; deleted only when nothing valid remains; never merged to another doc
File removed only after whole-repository reference check finds no uses (CI config, tests included)
Only git-tracked files deleted; untracked and ignored files reported, never deleted
Every removal writes recovery record: path, last commit, why
No superseded/archived banner, header or note added in place of correction or cut
Path doc names that no longer exists checked against git history before called drift
Each reviewed PRD, TRD and system-describing loose doc carries 'Where this lives in the code' section (directories, modules, symbols, no line numbers)
Review corrects code map along with rest of doc
After every run, PRD index and TRD index list every doc of its class in tree and nothing absent
Each index entry lists doc's path and top-level code directories from its map
Doc state visible expressed by file path not by text inside it
Run commits to new local branch from checked-out commit, prints push and PR command, does not push/merge
Change set lists corrections, cuts, removals with recovery records, each doc's score/depth, and every surfaced item
Run does not ask for confirmation of individual deletions; branch review is checkpoint
Claims about another repository's code reported in change set; not corrected, cut, or counted as drift
Assembly step (F1) makes no model call and is deterministic
Deterministic scripts are unit-tested
Review command emits standard status banners and four-section readout
No mid-run confirmation prompts, including none per deletion

tasks.description: Build packages/core/lib/docs-audit-assemble.js: inventory docs/, D3 classification (PRD folder + structure), git status, commit window, marker validation, per-doc windows, missing-path history via git, TRD parse via parseTrd, map detection, batching (200 doc cap), threshold read, per-batch workflow args. Jest tests on fixture trees and git repos; add packages/full/lib/ symlink.

Build packages/core/lib/docs-audit-apply.js: validate workflow records against batch doc list, revert stray edits, post-checks (banners, code maps), fixed-point reference check including CI/tests, tracked-only removal, recovery records (path, last commit, reason). Jest tests on fixture git repos; add packages/full/lib/ symlink.

Build packages/core/lib/docs-audit-deliver.js: prepare (clean tracked tree, create branch), commit-batch (stage applied edits and removals), finalize (regenerate indexes from tree state, write marker with HEAD, render change set, commit all, revert stray edits, switch back, print push/PR command). Jest tests on fixture git repos; add packages/full/lib/ symlink.

Build packages/core/workflows/audit-docs.js: Score phase (Haiku per PRD/TRD), Route phase (by thresholds), Review phase (parallel over per-doc thunks: Opus three verifiers + apply, Sonnet once-over, or none; loose sweep in comprehensive runs). Return { batch, records: [DocRecord], dead }. Test via test-harness.js.

Write packages/core/contracts/docs-audit.md: ten sections read by every reviewing agent: (1) Correct or cut section-by-section procedure, (2) No banners rule, (3) Absence must exhibit search, (4) Missing paths history check, (5) Cross-repo claims, (6) PRD procedure (built/different/unbuilt), (7) TRD procedure (tasks, status, unbuilt), (8) Loose-doc procedure, (9) Code map format/rules, (10) Return shape (DocRecord fields).

Write packages/core/commands/audit-docs.md per §3.6 (parse flags, prepare, assemble, loop per batch [Workflow call, apply, commit-batch, PHASE banner], finalize, publish change set artifact, readout, PushNotification, notify-complete.sh, delete work dir, COMMAND COMPLETE banner). Create dogfood copies: .claude/commands/audit-docs.md (mirror), .claude/workflows/audit-docs.js, .claude/contracts/docs-audit.md, .claude/lib/docs-audit-*.js. Add .trd-state/_docs-audit/work/ to .gitignore.

Seam test packages/core/workflows/audit-docs.seam.test.js: load audit-docs.js via test-harness.js, stub agents, construct fixture assembly.json matching spec, run workflow, write result to temp file, invoke apply and deliver against fixture git repo, assert: record shape accepted without adaptation, remove-proposed → recovery record in change set, edit → batch commit, no path outside batch accepted.

Add /audit-docs to both: packages/core/templates/process.md.template and .claude/rules/process.md. Add to workflow overview diagram at top, add per-command section with Purpose, Usage, Options table (--comprehensive flag), Output, Process sections. Document ensemble.docsAudit.thresholds setting with defaults high 70/medium 40.

[LIVE] test/integration/tests/audit-docs.test.sh: build fixture repo with: PRD (requirement built differently, requirement not built), TRD (wrong Status, unbuilt task), part-stale doc (one valid section survives), CI-only-referenced data file, untracked doc, cross-repo path claim, non-PRD file in docs/PRD/, runbook naming deleted component. Scaffold it. Run /audit-docs --comprehensive headless → assert COMMAND COMPLETE banner, no banners added, valid section survives, CI file listed as blocked, untracked untouched, recovery records exist, indexes match tree, marker on branch only. Run light with branch unmerged → same window re-covered. Clone after merge, run light → sees merged marker.

open_questions: OQ-1: What should a comprehensive run do? — RESOLVED 2026-10-03 by owner: no commit window; every PRD/TRD gets at least Sonnet, Opus where Haiku rates high; loose docs swept; first run comprehensive and batched
OQ-2: What are the high and medium thresholds? — RESOLVED 2026-09-27 by owner: defaults high ≥ 70, medium ≥ 40, overridable per project

OQ-3: What happens to a TRD for unbuilt work? — RESOLVED 2026-10-03 by owner: skip only when no implementation work or work clearly in flight; include if development tasks all done even if test/doc/infra tasks open (D19)
OQ-4: Did 'full audit with opus' mean existing /audit-prd//audit-trd? — No: as-built audit of same shape (D7, D8) — UNRESOLVED, TRD's decision per AC-F4.4/F5.3
OQ-5: How deep should loose docs be reviewed? — UNRESOLVED; assumed Sonnet once-over in comprehensive runs only, not scored
OQ-6: Should untracked or ignored docs be reviewed? — RESOLVED: No, inventoried and reported, never edited (AC-F1.4, AC-F7.4)
OQ-7: May run take over the checkout? — RESOLVED: Yes per PRD assumption of clean scheduled checkout; creates branch, switches back at end (D15)
OQ-8: What about existing archive folder like docs/TRD/completed/? — RESOLVED: reviewed in place; review never moves files between folders (D21)
OQ-9: Should references from state files (e.g. implement.json) block removal? — RESOLVED: Yes, every reference found anywhere blocks removal and is listed (D10)
